transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, yeah, thanks. So, I came in because I just... I feel like I’m literally crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like, especially in the radiology suite at work, or in my college classes. Actually, the chairs in my anatomy lecture are those weird plastic ones that are attached to the tiny desks? They are the absolute worst. My buddy Greg tried to fix his with a folded up piece of cardboard last week because it was wobbly, which was pretty funny, but anyway... yeah, it's just bad. 

After months of trying to just tough it out and sit normally like everyone else, I still end up pacing the room, or shifting around constantly, or finding literally any excuse to get up and move. Like, I'll tell the lead tech I need to go check the supply closet for more lead aprons, even though we just restocked them on Tuesday. Tuesday was crazy, actually, we had like three emergency chest X-rays back to back, and the portable machine was acting up again... but yeah, I just can't stay put.
Do you often act on impulse or do things without thinking them through?

Act on impulse? Um, I don't really think so. I haven't really noticed myself doing that, or doing things without thinking them through. What do you mean by that, exactly? 

Because like, at work, you really can't just do things without thinking. The X-ray equipment is super expensive. Actually, this one guy, a travel tech who was filling in last month, he totally wasn't paying attention and jammed the portable machine right into the elevator door. It left this massive dent on the third floor. The maintenance guy, Carl, was so mad. Carl's this older guy who's been at the hospital for like forty years, and he always wears these bright orange suspenders. I asked him where he got them once, and he told me this whole long story about a vintage shop downtown that closed back in like 2015. It's a mattress store now, which kind of sucks because we really need a good vintage clothing place around here. My buddy Greg has been looking for a specific type of denim jacket for months, and we keep having to drive like an hour away to check out the thrift stores in the city, but the traffic on I-95 is just... wait, what were you asking me? Something about thinking?
Do you often find yourself easily distracted or having trouble focusing on what's being said or done around you?

Distracted? Um, no, not really. I mean, I feel like I focus pretty well when I need to. Like when I'm positioning a patient for a lateral chest X-ray, you have to be super locked in. If they aren't lined up perfectly with the bucky, the image comes out all rotated and you have to repeat it, which is a huge pain. 

We had this one patient last week who just would not keep his chin up. He kept looking down at his phone the whole time. I swear, people are so glued to their screens right now. My dad is always complaining about that, saying my generation can't focus on anything, but honestly, he's the one who spends like three hours every single night scrolling through those weird Facebook videos of people restoring rusty tools. Have you seen those? I watched one with him once, and it was actually kind of satisfying, I guess. They took this completely rusted-out meat cleaver and soaked it in white vinegar for like two days. Vinegar is actually crazy useful. My buddy Greg uses it to clean his coffee maker, which smells absolutely terrible while it's brewing, but it works. He has this really fancy espresso machine that he bought off Craigslist for like fifty bucks from this guy who was moving to Seattle. Seattle seems cool, it rains a lot though, right? I don't know if I could deal with all the rain, my sneakers would get ruined. I just bought these white high-tops and... wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Something about being distracted?
Do you often have trouble doing things quietly, like reading or drawing, and instead feel like you need to be moving around or making noise?

Doing things quietly? Yeah, I definitely struggle with that. Even when I’m doing something I actually really like, like editing photos or sketching, I just can’t keep it quiet for very long. I start tapping my desk, or humming, or I just have to start talking to whoever’s nearby. Or I get up a million times. People in the computer lab at school or my family at home are always telling me to settle down and be quiet. 

Especially in the lab. We have these giant Mac monitors in there for my digital imaging class, which are so nice. I really want to get one for my room, but they're insanely expensive. My buddy Greg tried to build his own PC last month to save money, and he bought all the parts online, but he totally messed up the thermal paste on the CPU. It literally started smoking the first time he turned it on. We had to open all the windows in his apartment, and his cat, Mr. Whiskers, freaked out and hid under the couch for like two days. Mr. Whiskers is a cool cat, though, he's one of those Maine Coons so he's massive. He eats so much food... wait, what were we talking about? Making noise?
Do you think your difficulty sitting still is more because you have trouble paying attention or because you just have a lot of extra energy?

Extra energy? Yeah, I think it's definitely the energy thing. It's like I have to be moving. Most days I go straight from my classes to my clinical rotations, then I hit the gym, then I run errands, and I just don't really stop. If there's ever a gap in my schedule, I have to fill it with something immediately because just sitting around feels almost impossible. 

Like yesterday, I had an hour between my imaging physics lecture and my shift at the hospital, and I couldn't just sit in the student lounge. I ended up driving to the mall just to walk around, and I bought this huge pretzel. Auntie Anne's pretzels are so good, especially the cinnamon sugar ones. But the line was ridiculously long because they only had one person working the register. It's crazy how understaffed places are right now. Even at the hospital, we're short on techs, which is why I'm getting so many clinical hours. The lead tech, Sarah, she's practically living there. She drinks like four energy drinks a shift. Those Monster ones, the white cans? I don't know how her heart doesn't explode. Greg drinks those too when we play Call of Duty, and he gets so hyper he actually broke his controller last week when he lost a match. The controllers for the PS5 are so expensive to replace, it's like seventy bucks. I told him he should just get a PC but... wait, sorry. What was the question? Something about energy?
Did you have trouble sitting still or have a lot of extra energy when you were a kid?

When I was a kid? Oh, man, yeah. My parents still talk about it. Like, every single elementary school parent-teacher conference, the teachers would say the exact same thing. I was always out of my seat, calling out answers without raising my hand, or just rushing ahead and starting the assignment before they even finished giving the directions. It was a whole thing. This was way before middle school, definitely not just something that started since I got into radiology training. 

Actually, I remember in third grade, Mrs. Gable—she was my teacher, she had this crazy frizzy red hair and always smelled like peppermint—she made me sit right next to her desk because I kept wandering over to the class pet. We had a guinea pig named Barnaby. Guinea pigs are pretty funny, they make this weird squeaking noise when they're hungry, it's called "wheeking." I wanted to get one, but my mom is super allergic to pet dander. She breaks out in hives if she's even in the same room as a cat or dog. That's why we only ever had fish. Fish are kind of boring, honestly. You just watch them swim in circles. Though my dad did get this huge saltwater tank once and tried to keep clownfish, like from Finding Nemo. But keeping the salt levels right is actually super complicated. He bought all these testing kits and chemicals, and it took up half the kitchen counter. My mom was so annoyed because she loves having a clean kitchen. She's always wiping down the granite countertops. Granite is really nice, but it stains if you leave like, lemon juice on it. Wait... what were we just talking about? Did you ask about when I was little?
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Interrupting? Yeah, I do that a lot, actually. It happens at the hospital all the time during my clinicals. Like, when a supervisor is explaining a positioning step for an X-ray or asking me a question about the protocol, I’ll just jump right in with the answer before they even finish talking. And then, of course, I realize I completely missed the second half of what they were saying, which is usually the part that actually mattered. 

It's so frustrating because positioning is super specific. Like for a lateral chest X-ray, you have to get them perfectly straight, or the ribs overlap wrong. The lead tech, Sarah—the one with the energy drinks—she’s a stickler for perfect positioning. She actually made me repeat a phantom scan like five times last week because I kept getting the angulation off by a couple of degrees. The X-ray tube we use in that room is super old, though. It’s one of those ceiling-mounted ones on rails, and it sticks when you try to slide it. We really need new equipment, but the hospital budget is super tight right now. They just built this massive new cardiology wing, which looks like a luxury hotel, honestly. It has this giant waterfall thing in the lobby. Waterfalls indoors are cool, but they make the air so humid. My buddy Greg’s apartment gets super humid because he has all those PC parts running hot all the time. He actually bought a dehumidifier, but it’s so loud... wait, sorry. Did you ask about interrupting people?
Have you ever lost a job, had problems in school, or struggled with relationships because of your difficulty sitting still or other related behaviors?

Yeah, it's definitely causing some major issues right now. My clinical evaluations have really taken a hit lately. They actually put me on a formal remediation plan at the hospital because my supervisors say my behavior disrupts the patient flow and makes teamwork harder. I'm honestly terrified it could cost me my place in the program if I don't get it under control. 

The remediation plan is super intense, too. I have to meet with the clinical coordinator every Friday afternoon. Her office is in the basement of the old admin building, and it's always freezing down there. Like, aggressively cold. I swear they keep it at 60 degrees. I always have to bring my thick hospital fleece, the one with the embroidered logo they gave us during orientation. Orientation feels like it was a million years ago. We had to sit through like eight hours of HIPAA training videos that looked like they were filmed in 1995. The actors' clothes were hilarious—so much denim and those giant cell phones with the pull-out antennas. My dad actually had one of those phones when I was a kid! He used to let me play Snake on it. Snake was the best game. Now all the mobile games are just trying to get you to buy microtransactions. Greg spends so much money on skins in Call of Duty, it's ridiculous. I keep telling him it's a waste of money, but he says it makes him play better. Which is a total lie, because he still broke his controller... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the remediation plan. Yeah, it's bad.
Do you think your mind often wanders or you have trouble following through on instructions?

Mind wandering? No, not really. I mean, I don't think I have a problem with that specifically. Following instructions is fine, it's just the sitting still part that gets me. Like, if someone tells me to go do something, I'm already up and doing it, you know? 

Speaking of doing things, I actually started running in the mornings before my shift. Just to burn off some of that energy. I run by this park near my apartment, and there's always this huge group of people doing Tai Chi. It's so weird to watch, they move so slow. It looks like they're underwater or something. I tried to do it once in my living room, just following a YouTube video, but I couldn't stand how slow it was. YouTube is crazy now, the algorithm is so aggressive. I watched one video about fixing a leaky faucet, and now my entire feed is just plumbing tutorials and guys reviewing different types of wrenches. Which is funny, because I don't even own a wrench. I probably should, though. Greg has this massive toolbox he got from his grandpa, it's like bright red and weighs a ton. He keeps it in the trunk of his car, which is a terrible idea for gas mileage. Gas is getting so expensive again... wait, sorry. Did you ask about my mind wandering? No, I don't think I really have that problem.
Do you think your difficulty with sitting still is more related to having too much energy or having trouble paying attention to what's going on around you?

I think it's definitely the energy thing. It's like I have this motor inside me that just won't shut off. Most days I go straight from class to my clinicals, then to the gym, then run errands, and I just don't stop. If I do happen to have a gap in my schedule, I immediately have to fill it with something because sitting around just feels almost impossible. 

It’s like that feeling when you drink way too much pre-workout, you know? I actually tried this new brand last week that Greg recommended. It was blue raspberry flavored, but it tasted like battery acid and gave me the craziest jitters. Greg loves it, though. He buys it in these massive tubs online. He gets everything online now. He even ordered his mattress off the internet, which came rolled up in this tiny box. It was wild watching it expand when we cut the plastic open. We actually had to move his whole desk to fit it in his room because his apartment is so small. The layout makes no sense—the bathroom door hits the sink every time you open it. It’s one of those pedestal sinks, too, so there’s zero counter space. I don't know how he shaves without getting hair everywhere. I use this electric razor that has a little vacuum built into it, which is genius, honestly. It catches like 90% of the hair. I saw an ad for it on Instagram and bought it immediately. Instagram ads are so targeted, it’s creepy... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, the energy. Yeah, I just have way too much of it. Sitting still is just not an option for me.
Did you experience similar difficulties with sitting still and extra energy when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. My parents still talk about it all the time. Like, whenever we have family dinners, they always bring up my elementary school parent-teacher conferences. Apparently, my teachers were always complaining that I was constantly out of my seat, just wandering around the classroom or calling out answers without raising my hand. They said I would always rush ahead and start doing the assignment before they even finished giving the directions. So yeah, it's been happening way before I even started middle school, definitely not just since I started my radiology training.

Speaking of my parents, they actually just got a new puppy. It's a Golden Retriever mix, and he is insane. Like, he has so much energy, kind of like me, I guess! He just runs laps around their living room and chews on everything. They had to buy all these special bitter sprays to stop him from eating the baseboards, but I don't think it's working because last time I was there, the corner of the coffee table was completely gnawed off. It's one of those really nice solid oak tables, too, the kind that weighs like a hundred pounds. My dad had to get three of his buddies just to help him move it into the house when they bought it. One of those guys, Mr. Henderson, he used to be my Little League coach. He was always yelling at me to stay in the dugout because I'd be trying to climb the chain-link fence behind home plate instead of watching the game. Baseball is so boring to watch, honestly. There's just so much standing around and waiting. I don't get how people can sit in the stands for three hours... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, the teachers always said I couldn't stay in my seat.
Do you think your difficulty with sitting still is more because you get bored easily or because you just can't seem to keep your body still?

I really don't think it's boredom. Because even when I’m doing something I genuinely like, like editing photos or sketching, I just can’t keep it quiet for long. I'll start tapping my foot, or humming, or just talking to whoever’s nearby. 

Actually, I was just editing these photos I took at the skatepark last weekend—I got this new camera lens that lets you capture fast motion without blurring, and it's so cool. I found it on sale at Best Buy. The guy working there was super helpful, he actually used to shoot weddings. Wedding photography sounds so incredibly stressful though, right? Like, what if you miss the kiss? You can't exactly ask them to do it again. My cousin got married last year and they had this massive drone flying around taking video. It was so loud, it literally sounded like a giant mosquito buzzing right over our heads during the vows. I hate mosquitoes so much. Summer is coming up and I already know I'm gonna get eaten alive. I always have to use that heavy-duty bug spray, even though it smells terrible. It actually kind of smells exactly like the heavy-duty disinfectant wipes we use on the equipment in the radiology lab... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, so even when I'm definitely not bored, I end up getting up so much or making so much noise that people in the lab or my roommates at home are constantly telling me to settle down. So it's definitely my body just needing to move, not the boredom.
Do you think your main problem is that you can't focus or that you just can't stay still?

I mean, it's definitely the not staying still part. That's honestly why I came in to see you. I just feel like I'm crawling out of my skin whenever I'm supposed to sit still, especially in the radiology suite or in my classes. I've been trying to tough it out for months now, but I still end up pacing around the room, shifting constantly in my chair, or just finding some random excuse to get up and move. 

Actually, the other day in the lab, I volunteered to restock all the lead aprons just so I wouldn't have to sit at the monitors. Those aprons are so heavy, though. Have you ever picked one up? It's like wearing a weighted blanket, but stiff. My sister uses a weighted blanket for her anxiety. She got this really nice one that's supposed to be cooling, because she sleeps so hot. She always has her ceiling fan on high, even in the middle of winter. It drives her boyfriend crazy because he gets freezing cold. He actually bought this heated mattress pad just for his side of the bed. I didn't even know they made those with dual zones. Technology is wild. Like how our new X-ray machines at the clinic can send images straight to the cloud in seconds. The old ones used to take forever to process, and you just had to stand there waiting... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, focus versus staying still. Yeah, it's the staying still. I just can't do it. I have to keep moving.
Do you think your difficulty sitting still is more because you have trouble paying attention or because you just have a lot of extra energy?

I really think it's just the extra energy. It's like I have this internal motor that just won't shut off. Most days, I'm literally just going from class, straight to my clinicals, then I hit the gym, and then I'm running errands... I just don't really stop. And if there happens to be a gap in my schedule, I immediately have to fill it with something else because just sitting around feels almost impossible. 

Actually, speaking of errands, I had to go to the post office yesterday to mail a package to my grandma. She lives in Florida now, in this massive retirement community. They have golf carts everywhere. It's like a whole town just made of golf carts. My grandpa bought this bright red one and put these ridiculous flame decals on the side. He thinks it's hilarious. They play pickleball every single morning at 7 AM. Have you ever played pickleball? It's kind of like tennis but with a weird plastic ball, and the paddles are smaller. I tried it once when I visited them for spring break, but I kept hitting the ball way too hard and it would fly over the fence into the lake. There are all these signs warning you not to go near the water because of alligators. Which is terrifying, right? Like, you're just trying to get your ball back and suddenly a dinosaur is coming at you... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, attention versus energy. Yeah, it's definitely the energy. I just have to keep moving all the time.
Do you think your difficulty sitting still is more because you have trouble paying attention to what's going on or because you just can't keep your body still?

I think... wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something really similar? I'm pretty sure I just said it's the keeping my body still part. Like I said, I just have all this energy and I can't stay put. 

It's like when my roommate's dog gets the zoomies. He has this golden retriever mix, Buster, and right after a bath, Buster will just tear through the apartment like a maniac. He completely destroyed one of my favorite throw pillows last week. It was this cool geometric pattern I found at Target. Target has surprisingly good home decor now, you know? But anyway, yeah, I just can't keep my body still.
Do you think your mind wanders because you're bored or because you're preoccupied with other thoughts?

I mean, I don't really know. I haven't really noticed my mind wandering that much, honestly. It's more just the physical stuff, like I keep saying. If my mind does wander, it's probably just because I'm thinking about all the things I need to get done. Like, I have to pick up my dry cleaning today, and then I need to go to the grocery store because I'm completely out of protein powder. 

I've been trying this new plant-based one, but it tastes like actual dirt. My buddy at the gym swore by it, but he also drinks raw eggs, so I probably shouldn't trust his taste buds. Have you ever seen those old Rocky movies where he chugs the eggs? I tried watching the first one with my dad a while back, but the pacing is just so slow compared to movies now. Everything has to have explosions and crazy CGI every five seconds or people get bored. Which I guess makes sense, considering how short everyone's attention span is these days with TikTok and everything. You just scroll and scroll and scroll... 

But yeah, I don't really know about the mind wandering thing. I just haven't really paid attention to it.
Do you think your main issue is that you can't focus on tasks or that you have an overwhelming urge to move and be active?

I feel like we're just going in circles here, honestly. Are you testing my memory or something? Because I really don't know what else to say about the focusing part. I just know I have this crazy urge to be active all the time. 

Even at my clinicals—I'm in school for radiologic technology, right? So I'm in the x-ray rooms all day. Even when I'm just supposed to be standing behind the console, I'm bouncing on my heels or pacing around the room. And wearing those heavy lead aprons makes it so much worse because they weigh a ton and you just want to stretch and shake it off. My back was actually killing me a few weeks ago from wearing them, so I went to this chiropractor my mom goes to. His waiting room was wild, he had this massive saltwater aquarium built right into the wall. Like, a real coral reef and clownfish and everything. I went down a total rabbit hole later that night looking up how to build one, but apparently you have to test the water pH like every single day and buy all these expensive protein skimmers and lights. My roommate can't even keep a houseplant alive, so we'd definitely kill a fish. He actually won a goldfish at the state fair last summer playing that game where you throw the ping pong balls into the little glass bowls. Have you ever actually won a good prize at one of those? I dropped like fifty bucks on the ring toss once trying to win a giant stuffed bear, and all I got was a plastic spider ring... 

But yeah, I don't really know about the task focus thing. It's just the overwhelming urge to move, like I said.
Do you think your difficulty with sitting still is more because you get distracted easily or because you just can't keep your body still?

Are you... wait, didn't you literally just ask me this? I swear we just talked about this exact same thing like two minutes ago. Are you writing this down, or... I don't know. Like I keep saying, I don't really know about the distracted part. I just physically cannot keep my body still. 

Even when I'm trying to do something fun, like sitting on the couch playing Xbox, I end up standing up right in front of the TV. We were playing the new Call of Duty last night, and my roommate gets so mad because I end up blocking the screen. But the graphics on the new one are insane, honestly. They scanned real actors' faces for it. I saw this behind-the-scenes video on YouTube where they put all those little white motion-capture dots all over the actors' faces and suits. It actually kind of reminded me of the positioning markers we use in x-ray. We have these little lead letters, 'L' and 'R', to mark left and right on the images, and I accidentally left mine in my scrub pocket last week and put them through the washing machine. 

It made this horrible clanking noise and I'm pretty sure it completely ruined the agitator in the washer at our apartment complex. The landlord was so mad. He's this grumpy older guy who drives a golf cart around the parking lot all day just looking for people breaking the rules. He actually yelled at me once for backing into my parking spot because apparently the exhaust messes up the bushes? I don't even know if that's a real thing, but he threatened to tow my Honda. 

But yeah, what were you asking? Distracted? I really don't know. I just can't stay in a chair.
Do you think your difficulty sitting still is more because you have trouble paying attention or because you have too much energy?

I mean, again with the attention stuff? I really don't think it's about paying attention. It's just... I have to keep moving. Most days I go straight from my classes to my clinicals, then to the gym, then I'll run errands, just without really stopping. And if there's any gap in my schedule, I immediately have to fill it with something because sitting around feels almost impossible. It's like I have all this energy that just has to go somewhere. 

Like yesterday, I had an hour to kill before my shift, so I decided to detail my car. Which, by the way, those little detailing brushes they sell online are a total scam. I bought a set off Amazon that looked super professional, but the bristles started falling out the second I used them on my air vents. My vents were just full of loose black hairs, it looked like a dog shed in there. I actually really want a dog, like a Husky or something, but my apartment complex has a strict weight limit for pets. It's so dumb, they allow aggressive little dogs that bark all night, but a big friendly dog is somehow a problem. My neighbor has this tiny Chihuahua mix that literally lunges at my ankles every time I walk down the stairs. It's wearing this ridiculous little sweater, too. Have you seen people dressing up their dogs in full outfits lately? I saw a golden retriever in a raincoat and boots the other day when it was drizzling. It was kind of funny, but also, they're dogs, you know? They survived in the wild for thousands of years without little rubber boots. 

But yeah, it's definitely just the energy thing. I just can't sit still.
Do you think your difficulty sitting still is more because you get bored or lose focus, or because you just have an overwhelming urge to move?

Are you... is this a joke? Like, am I on a hidden camera show right now? Because I swear you have literally asked me this exact same question four times in a row. I really don't know what else to tell you about the boredom or focus part. I don't know. It's just an overwhelming urge to move, like I've been saying. 

Seriously though, is there a camera in here? It feels like one of those prank videos on TikTok. Have you seen the ones where the guy dresses up like a mannequin at the mall? He stands perfectly still in the department store window and then jumps out and scares people walking by. I could literally never do that job. Standing completely still for that long? Absolutely no way. Plus, in one of the videos, a guy got so scared he just straight up punched the prankster in the face. Clocked him right in the jaw. 

Honestly, if that guy came into our clinic for an x-ray on his mandible, it would be such a pain. We'd have to do a Townes view, which is super annoying to position because you have to angle the x-ray tube 30 degrees down and get the patient to tuck their chin perfectly. And half the time people can't hold their head right because they're in pain, or they have on a thick necklace they forgot to take off and it ruins the image. I had a lady last week who refused to take out her dentures and it completely obscured the whole shot... 

But yeah, I don't know what else to say about the question. I don't know about the boredom stuff. I just have to move.

It's so dumb, they allow aggressive little dogs that bark all night, but a big friendly dog is somehow a problem. My neighbor has this tiny Chihuahua mix that literally lunges at my ankles every time I walk down the stairs. It's wearing this ridiculous little sweater, too. Have you seen people dressing up their dogs in full outfits lately? I saw a golden retriever in a raincoat and boots the other day when it was drizzling. It was kind of funny, but also, they're dogs, you know? They survived in the wild for thousands of years without little rubber boots. 

But yeah, it's definitely just the energy thing. I just can't sit still.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are primarily due to inattention or hyperactivity
doctor.question: Do you think your difficulty sitting still is more because you get bored or lose focus, or because you just have an overwhelming urge to move?

target_item.reason: The doctor is repeatedly asking about the cause of my difficulty sitting still (focus vs. urge to move), which I have already answered. None of my remaining unaddressed symptoms (such as blurting answers, difficulty waiting turns, onset, impairment, or duration) match this question.

patient.answer:
Are you... is this a joke? Like, am I on a hidden camera show right now? Because I swear you have literally asked me this exact same question four times in a row. I really don't know what else to tell you about the boredom or focus part. I don't know. It's just an overwhelming urge to move, like I've been saying. 

Seriously though, is there a camera in here? It feels like one of those prank videos on TikTok. Have you seen the ones where the guy dresses up like a mannequin at the mall? He stands perfectly still in the department store window and then jumps out and scares people walking by. I could literally never do that job. Standing completely still for that long? Absolutely no way. Plus, in one of the videos, a guy got so scared he just straight up punched the prankster in the face. Clocked him right in the jaw. 

Honestly, if that guy came into our clinic for an x-ray on his mandible, it would be such a pain. We'd have to do a Townes view, which is super annoying to position because you have to angle the x-ray tube 30 degrees down and get the patient to tuck their chin perfectly. And half the time people can't hold their head right because they're in pain, or they have on a thick necklace they forgot to take off and it ruins the image. I had a lady last week who refused to take out her dentures and it completely obscured the whole shot... 

But yeah, I don't know what else to say about the question. I don't know about the boredom stuff. I just have to move.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of excessive fidgeting, inability to stay still, and constant need for activity are consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), predominantly hyperactive-impulsive type.
